tagline: OV-101 — prototype Shuttle. Renamed from Constitution after Star Trek fan campaign. Flew 1977 atmospheric tests; never reached orbit
description: Originally called Constitution, renamed Enterprise after a fan-letter campaign tied to Star Trek's 10th anniversary. Built as a prototype for the Approach and Landing Tests (ALT) — eight captive flights and five free flights from the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft over Edwards Air Force Base in 1977. First free flight 1977-08-12 piloted by Fred Haise + Gordon Fullerton proved the orbiter could glide and land. Did NOT contain propulsion or active TPS tiles; converting Enterprise to flight-rated was estimated heavier than building a new orbiter from structural spares, so Challenger was built instead. Now on display at the Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum in NYC.
best_known_for: Prototype Shuttle; 1977 atmospheric drop tests; never flew to orbit
